title: CHAPTER NINE. On the forensic law: definition
latin: CAPUT NONUM. De lege forensi. Lex FORENSIS est ordinatio, quam Deus per Mosen populo Israelitico praescripsit, & per eius successores repetivit & accommodavit, continens praecepta de forma gubernationis politicae in civili societate usurpandae, ad bonum vitae tum animalis tum etiam spiritualis procurandum per conservationem & exactionem cultus externi & disciplinae externae lege morali & cerimoniali praescriptae. Haec lex potissimum agit de magistratibus, contractibus, bonorum divisionibus, iudiciis, poenis & similibus (Exod. 21–23; Deut. 17). Referri potest ad duo genera: prius iuris communis quoad substantiam; posterius iuris singularis ad solam Judaeorum remp.
english: CHAPTER NINE. On the forensic law.

The FORENSIC law is an ordinance God prescribed through Moses to Israel and repeated through his successors, containing precepts on the form of political government in civil society, for procuring animal and spiritual life-goods by conserving the external worship and discipline of the moral and ceremonial law.

It chiefly treats magistrates, contracts, divisions of goods, judgments, and penalties (Exod. 21–23; Deut. 17). It has two genera: common right as to substance, and singular right belonging to the Jewish commonwealth alone.

It has two genera: common right as toward substance, and singular right belonging toward ye Jewish commonwealth alone. — Ye FORENSIC law stands as an ordinance God prescribed through Moses toward Israel and repeated through his successors, containing precepts on ye form belonging toward political government in civil society, for procuring animal and spiritual life-goods by conserving ye external worship and discipline belonging toward ye moral and ceremonial law. — CHAPTER NINE. On ye forensic law.

title: II–III. Threefold use of the forensic law
latin: II. Est vero etiam hic legis forensis observandus usus & abrogatio. III. Usus vero illius legis triplex est: primus, ut totus status populi Judaici certa norma publicae aequitatis & iustitiae ordinaretur; secundus, ut populus iste ab aliis populis etiam hac lege discriminaretur; tertius ad ea respexit quae futura erant, & fuit typus. Primus usus colligitur ex Ps. 122:3-8. Alter fluit ex eo quod Deus voluit populum suum nihil cum aliis commune habere ubi fieri poterat (Ps. 2; Ezek. 34:23-24). De tertio non est dubium quin totus status & regnum Judaicum Christum eiusque regnum spirituale adumbraverint. Hoc respectu lex forensis paedagogus ad Christum dici meretur.
english: II–III. Its use is threefold: first, that the Jewish people's whole state might be ordered by a norm of public equity and justice; second, that this people might be distinguished by this law from other peoples; third, that it looked to future things and was a type.

The first use is gathered from Psalm 122:3-8. The second flows from God's will that His people share nothing needless with others (Ps. 2; Ezek. 34:23-24). As to the third, that whole Jewish state and kingdom shadowed Christ and His spiritual kingdom. In this respect the forensic law also deserves to be called a pedagogue to Christ.

title: IV. Abrogation; Cap.10 next on the Gospel
latin: IV. Abrogatio legis forensis non quidem tollit communem aequitatem in ipso naturae lumine fundatam; quatenus tamen Christum respexit, abrogata est haec lex universe. Quantum ad simplicem observationem, neque prohibita est neque praescripta ulli populo absoluta necessitate, si excipiantur quae communis iuris sunt & naturali aequitate nituntur. Quae vero quoad substantiam & finem praecipuum in Christum respiciunt, nulli populo licet usurpare. Huc refer Josephum, Philonem, Maimonidem, Sigonium, Bertramum, & Petrum Cunaeum de republica Judaeorum. CAPUT DECIMUM sequitur, De Euangelio: ubi de Symbolo Apostolorum.
english: IV. Abrogation does not remove the common equity founded in nature's light; yet insofar as the law looked to Christ, it is abrogated universally.

Simple observation is neither forbidden nor absolutely prescribed to any people, except what rests on common right and natural equity. What as to substance and chief end looks to Christ, no people may usurp. Refer Josephus, Philo, Maimonides, Sigonius, Bertram, and Cunaeus On the Jewish Commonwealth.
CHAPTER TEN follows, On the Gospel: where also on the Apostles' Creed.
